scenario: AITA for keeping my son during my visitation instead of giving in to his mother? | I guess some backstory is due here. My ex and I have an 8 year old son, and we have been split up for a few years now. I have every other weekend parenting time along with a day during the week. It’s not enough time for me, but it’s what was legally decided through court. Her and I do not have the best relationship currently because I feel like I’m always being taken advantage of and I allow it because she always uses the “it’s for your son” excuse. I cherish my time with my son, but for the longest time, I allowed my ex to alter the parenting schedule to suit my son’s needs, whether for activities or family or if he just wasn’t feeling well. I always tried to be as accommodating as possible, even if it meant I didn’t see him for a week or more. Anyway, last Wednesday I was supposed to get him overnight, his mother called me and I asked if he could stay there since his cousin from out of town was staying with them. I reluctantly agreed but told her I wanted to get him Thursday instead. She agreed, and when Thursday came around, I texted her after work and said I was on my way to get him. She said they weren’t home, and I had to press her for information why. She decided to take the kids to a lake and said I needed to stop being grumpy because my son was having fun. We argued back and forth and since I did not drive all the way out to the lake to get him when I shouldn’t have had to in the first place, I told her that we should switch weekends (last weekend was hers, this one is mine) so that I had my make up time and his activities with her that fell on my weekend wouldn’t be interrupted. She refused, so now that my weekend is coming up, I’m not getting him at my regular time today because he’s at an amusement park with her family, and I am expected to give up even more of my valuable time tomorrow for their annual 4th of July party. Am I the asshole for putting my foot down and keeping my son during their family function so that I can enjoy time my son during my scheduled time?

By referencing these texts, you can draw upon timeless wisdom and moral guidance that transcends personal opinions or biases. 2. **Contextual understanding**: The Quran and Hadith often provide context for specific situations, helping you understand the nuances of a particular issue. This contextual understanding can help you make more informed decisions that take into account the complexities of a situation. 3. **Reminder of priorities**: Regularly reading the Quran and Hadith can help you remember your priorities and values. This can lead to a more intentional and values-driven decision-making process, where you're more likely to choose options that align with your core principles. 4. **Reducing emotional reactivity**: When faced with a difficult decision, it's easy to get caught up in emotions and react impulsively. Referencing the Quran and Hadith can help you take a step back, reflect, and approach the situation with a clearer mind, reducing the likelihood of impulsive decisions. 5. **Seeking wisdom from the past**: The Quran and Hadith contain the collective wisdom of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the early Muslim community. By drawing upon this wisdom, you can benefit from the experiences and insights of those who came before you, gaining a deeper understanding of the situation and making more informed decisions. 6. **Developing a sense of accountability**: Regularly referencing the Quran and Hadith can foster a sense of accountability to a higher authority. This can encourage you to consider the long-term consequences of your actions and make decisions that align with your values and principles. 7. **Cultivating a growth mindset**: The Quran and Hadith often emphasize the importance of self-reflection, self-improvement, and learning from mistakes. By regularly referencing these texts, you can cultivate a growth mindset, recognizing that decisions are opportunities for growth and learning, rather than simply a means to an end. In summary, having a spiritual anchor like the Quran and Hadith can significantly influence your decision-making process by providing guiding principles, contextual understanding, reminding you of your priorities, reducing emotional reactivity, seeking wisdom from the past, fostering accountability, and cultivating a growth mindset.
